drafted_from: tool row in tools/track-and-compare-movement/tool-rows.json, do-work/align_dtw.py and test/test_align_dtw.py (run on its synthetic skeletons)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Line up my serve track /work/poses/mine.json with the reference /work/poses/coach.json and write the alignment to /work/align/mine-vs-coach.json, soft warping 0.1." It reads the tool's row and runs align_dtw.py on your computer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads video or pose files on the person's own computer and writes a new file or folder beside them.
instructions: 1. Make a pose track for each movement with tool:read-peoples-poses-from-a-video (any pose.keypoints.v1 file works).

2. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:line-up-two-movements} and runs its `run` command with --clip, --reference, --out and --gamma (0 for hard warping, 0.1 if you say nothing); numpy is the only package needed.

3. Read the last line: {"result": {out, clip_frames, reference_frames, path_length, distance}}. The file holds the path of [clip_index, reference_index] pairs; each pair shows the same phase of the movement. distance is comparable across references.
4. Use the path to show the same phase side by side (tool:plan-a-side-by-side-movement-comparison). The match is on body posture only; it does not say which movement is better.

worked_examples.title: Align a 30 frame swing with a slower 45 frame swing
worked_examples.ask: Line up my swing track with the coach's and write the alignment.
worked_examples.given: From tools/track-and-compare-movement/test/test_align_dtw.py (test_phase_aligns_different_speeds), which I ran to observe the answer. The clip track has 30 frames of a wrist swinging on a sine; the reference has 45 frames, slower and shifted in phase. Command: python3 tools/track-and-compare-movement/do-work/align_dtw.py --clip /work/poses/mine.json --reference /work/poses/coach.json --out /work/align/mine-vs-coach.json --gamma 0.1.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"out": "/work/align/mine-vs-coach.json", "clip_frames": 30, "reference_frames": 45, "path_length": 73, "distance": 0.123625}} The file has kind phase_alignment.v1, the model note soft-DTW (gamma=0.1) over hip-centered torso-scaled COCO-17 features, and a path of 73 pairs that starts [0, 0], [1, 0], [2, 1], [3, 1] and ends [29, 42], [29, 43], [29, 44]: time never runs backwards and every frame of both clips appears.
